findings.comment: Transformer pad set-up areas are not dimensioned on the submitted electrical plan. No 20-foot by 35-foot clear zones are identified or called out in front of the four transformer pads shown, nor is the required 35-foot vertical clearance documented. Provide dimensioned set-up area callouts on electrical and site plans.

applicableAreas: Truck access paths to all four transformer pads
findings.comment: Truck access path widths are not dimensioned on the site plan or electrical plan. The internal concrete drive providing access to transformer pads does not have a specified minimum 12-foot horizontal width dimension. Provide width dimension callout for access routes to each transformer pad.

applicableAreas: Vertical clearance zones above all transformer pads and access routes
findings.comment: Vertical clearance above truck access paths to transformer pads is not documented on submitted plans. No dimension callouts show 16-foot minimum vertical clearance from finished surface to overhead obstructions (buildings, eaves, overhangs, utility lines). Provide vertical clearance cross-sections or elevation callouts.

applicableAreas: Concrete drive access surfaces to all transformer pads
findings.comment: Pavement structural design calculations are not provided for the concrete drive serving transformer pad access. The site plan notes 'Concrete Drive' and 'Concrete Curb' but provides no structural calculations demonstrating the pavement can support 72,180 lbs total vehicle weight with maximum 32,530 lbs rear axle weight. Provide pavement structural design calculations per UCM requirements.

applicableAreas: Western entry area near Transformer Pad 1 (west of Building 1)
findings.comment: An 18-inch grate inlet (Rim elevation 683.08) is located in the drive aisle near Building 1, in close proximity to Transformer Pad 1. The spatial relationship between the storm inlet and the transformer pad is not clearly documented on the site plan with dimensions. Verify inlet does not block truck access curb in front of transformer pad; provide dimensioned clearance callout if inlet is adjacent to transformer access.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 1 (NW near western entry and Building 1)
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 1 is surrounded by proposed landscaping and tree features including a labeled 'Tree Well' immediately adjacent, and dense Street Yard landscaping (H-3) in the western entry area. The pad is shown situated within tree/landscaping symbols but no clear access zone is maintained demonstrating 24/7 accessibility for Austin Energy maintenance. Remove trees and landscaping from 10-foot radius around transformer pad or provide AE Design approval of alternative clearance arrangement.

applicableAreas: Relationship between transformer pads and fire lanes
findings.comment: Fire lanes are marked on the internal driveway loop serving transformer pads (fire lanes shown on northern and southern straightaways). However, transformer pad locations are not called out on the fire protection plan, making it unclear whether any pads are actually located within or obstructing fire lanes. Identify transformer pad locations on fire protection plan and verify none are in fire lanes or note any fire lane coordination approved by AE.

Multiple transformer pads lack direct line of sight to associated meters due to building geometry: Transformer 1 (west of Bldg 1) blocked from north wall meters by building corner; Transformer 3 blocked from north wall meters of Bldgs 3 and 4; Transformer 4 blocked from west wall meters of Bldg 6. Provide unobstructed line of sight from all transformers to meters or document written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering if line of sight exceptions are necessary.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing paths from transformers to meters
findings.comment: Electrical routing between transformers, pull boxes, and meters is shown with dashed blue lines, but the number and location of 90-degree bends/turns are not explicitly documented or counted on the plan. Trace and count routing turns on electrical plan; provide documentation that maximum two 90-degree bends are not exceeded in any transformer-to-meter routing path.

Clearances between electrical conduit routing and drainage infrastructure (pipes, grate inlets, manholes) are not dimensioned or documented. An 18-inch grate inlet (Rim 683.08) is located near Transformer Pad 1. Overlay electrical and drainage plans with dimension callouts showing minimum 12-inch clearance from electrical routing to all drainage infrastructure.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pads 2 and 3 (adjacent to parking areas)
findings.comment: Transformer Pads 2 and 3 are located directly adjacent to perpendicular parking spaces (within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas). No bollard specifications or callouts are shown on the electrical or site plans. Provide 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollard specifications and location callouts for all transformer pads within 4 feet of parking areas, spacing bollards to allow equipment door opening.

Minimum 2-foot clearance from transformer pads to back of sidewalks is not dimensioned on submitted plans. Provide dimension callouts on site plan showing minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalk to back of each transformer pad.

Multiple meter locations are not within direct sight of their associated transformer pads (per EL-14.38 finding), and no written approval from AE Design and Distribution Metering business units is documented on submitted plans. Provide line of sight from transformer to meter or document written approval from both AE Design and Distribution Metering if sight line exception is requested and approved.

applicableAreas: Set-up areas and clearances at all transformer pads
findings.comment: Transformer pad set-up areas (20 ft × 35 ft with 35-foot vertical clearance) are not dimensioned on submitted plans, and no documented AE Design approval of any deviations from standard clearance requirements is provided. Provide either compliant set-up area dimensions on all plans or document written AE Design approval of specific project deviations with conditions.
